items.headline: Kan poll puts Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats, the opposition at 50
items.summary: The Kan public broadcaster published a Kantar poll on Sunday evening (552 respondents, margin of error 4.2 points).

items.headline: Bennett floats, then withdraws, a role for Netanyahu in a future government
items.summary: Also on Sunday, Bennett told a conference of the religious Zionist paper HaDor that Netanyahu could join a future government, and even be a minister, if he accepted the bloc's guidelines, including a state commission of inquiry into 7 October.
items.source: Times of Israel Times of Israel

items.headline: Polymarket moves toward Eisenkot despite the Kan poll
items.summary: Polymarket moved against the Kan poll.

items.headline: Al Arabiya: Washington to announce progress on the Lebanon framework this week
items.summary: Al Arabiya's Washington correspondent, Pierre Ghanem, reported on Sunday that the State Department intends to announce progress this week on the three-way framework between the United States, Lebanon and Israel.

items.headline: An-Nahar: detained men say the Dahr al-Baidar explosives belong to Hezbollah
items.summary: An-Nahar reported new details on the 500 kilograms of explosives (250 of TNT and 250 of C-4) seized at Dahr al-Baidar.

items.headline: Two olive harvesters killed in south Lebanon; Israeli strikes on three villages
items.summary: In the south, two men harvesting olives were killed on Sunday, a retired soldier near Yater by Israeli artillery and an engineer in Froun by an old munition.

items.headline: Lula holds his largest rally; Flávio Bolsonaro warns allies that "nothing is settled"
items.summary: Lula held his largest rally of the campaign on Sunday on the Avenida Paulista in São Paulo.

items.headline: DataTrends poll has Flávio ahead; he leads in four of five main polls
items.summary: A smaller pollster, DataTrends, published a poll on Sunday (2,000 automated telephone interviews, 7–9 October, margin of error 2.2 points) with Flávio at 50% and Lula at 44%, or 53.1% to 46.9% in valid votes (GP1).

items.headline: Colombia's government turns toward Israel; Jerusalem embassy opens 14 October
items.summary: El País reports that Colombia's interior minister, Rodrigo Lara, spoke at last Wednesday's 7 October memorial at the Centro Israelita in Bogotá, the first time the national government has attended.

items.headline: Musk says Starship Flight 15 will try to catch the upper stage
items.summary: Speaking by video at the X Takeover fan event in Texas on Saturday, Musk said that Starship Flight 15 will try to catch the upper stage with the launch tower, which would be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket, and that he hopes it will fly in four to six weeks, "a little bit before Thanksgiving." These are his claims.

items.headline: EU sets up a training mission for Lebanon's army and police as UNIFIL prepares to leave
items.summary: On 12 October, EU foreign ministers set up the EU Support Mission in Lebanon (EUSM Lebanon), with an initial mandate of three years.
items.source: Council of the EU Euronews Asharq Al-Awsat Rapporteur

items.headline: Grok Bot 0.70.2: Bots get their own email addresses and can search X
items.summary: Version 0.70.2, released on 11 October, lets a Bot claim its own email address and receive mail there.

items.headline: Grok Bot 0.68: slide decks, formatted email and Gmail send-as addresses
items.summary: Version 0.68.0 (5 October) lets email drafts go out from a verified Gmail send-as address and adds five languages: Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Swahili and Hausa.
items.source: Grok Bot changelog (official) Grok Bot Wiki

items.headline: Grok Bot 0.66–0.67: the primary Bot offers to take on work; Marketplace becomes Connect Apps
items.summary: Version 0.66.0 (2 October) lets the user's primary Bot, the one marked with a star, notice work it could take on and offer to do it.
items.source: Grok Bot changelog (official) Grok Bot Wiki

items.headline: Channel 12 poll: Eisenkot's bloc 54, Netanyahu's 49; Winter again below the threshold
items.summary: A Channel 12 Midgam poll published on Monday evening (509 respondents, margin of error 4.4 points) again put Gadi Eisenkot's bloc at 54 seats and Benjamin Netanyahu's at 49.

items.headline: Channel 14 poll: Netanyahu's bloc at 62; Bennett rises to 11 seats
items.summary: A Channel 14 / Next Data poll published on Wednesday (568 adults, 14 October) gives the right-wing bloc 62 seats, the left-center bloc 44 and the Arab parties 14.

items.headline: Ben-Gvir refuses a surplus-vote deal with Ofer Winter
items.summary: National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir said on Tuesday that Otzma Yehudit would not sign a surplus-vote agreement with Ofer Winter's Amcha Yisrael.

items.headline: Polymarket: Eisenkot about 48%, Netanyahu about 27%, Bennett about 14%
items.summary: On Polymarket, Eisenkot is now at about 48% to be the next sworn-in prime minister, Netanyahu at about 27% and Bennett at about 14%.

items.headline: Katz: if Hezbollah joins an Iranian attack, Israel will take more land around Nabatieh and the Litani
items.summary: Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Wednesday, during a visit to the IDF buffer zone in southern Lebanon, that if Hezbollah joins Iran in an attack on Israel, it will lose more territory around Nabatieh and the Litani River as part of a permanent Israeli security zone.

items.headline: Quaest's first runoff poll: Flávio 46%, Lula 44%, a technical tie
items.summary: Quaest's first national runoff poll, published on Wednesday for Globo and O Globo (2,154 interviews, 10–13 October, margin of error 2 points), has Flávio Bolsonaro at 46% and Lula at 44%.

items.headline: Colombia opens its embassy in Jerusalem; Sa'ar and Bula preside
items.summary: Colombia inaugurated its embassy in Jerusalem on Wednesday 14 October, becoming the tenth country with an embassy in the city.

items.headline: Cursor opens an Origin App Marketplace with more than 20 partner apps
items.summary: On 13 October Cursor's changelog announced an Origin App Marketplace with more than 20 apps for deployments, CI, code review, security, monitoring and project management.

items.headline: Parti Québécois MNAs to be sworn in today; cabinet due 21 October
items.summary: The 59 newly elected Parti Québécois members of Quebec's National Assembly are to be sworn in on Thursday 15 October; Liberal opposition members on 19 October; and the PQ cabinet on 21 October.

items.headline: Zman Yisrael poll: Yashar 26, Likud 20; blocs still 54–49
items.summary: A Zman Yisrael poll for the Times of Israel, fielded on 14–15 October (500 respondents, margin of error 4.4 points), gives Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar 26 seats and Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud 20.

items.headline: Channel 13 Madad poll: Netanyahu bloc 51, Eisenkot 50; Hendel and Winter both at 4
items.summary: Channel 13's Madad poll (Shmuel Rosner and Noah Slepkov, 1,018 respondents, margin of error 3.1 points, fielded 13 October) puts Netanyahu's bloc at 51 seats and Eisenkot's at 50, with Arab parties at 15.

items.headline: Netanyahu: Defense and National Security stay with Likud; Otzma fires back
items.summary: At a campaign event in Acre on Thursday, Netanyahu said that if he forms the next government, Likud will keep the National Security and Education ministries, and repeated that Itamar Ben-Gvir will not be defense minister.

items.headline: EUSM Lebanon: Italy, France and Spain expected to supply most of about 100 troops
items.summary: Reporting on the force plan for the EU Support Mission in Lebanon (established by the Council on 12 October) says Italy, France and Spain are expected to provide most of a permanent military component of about 100 personnel, based mainly in Beirut, with no planned deployment to southern Lebanon near the Israeli border.

items.headline: Datafolha: Flávio 47%, Lula 45% in the runoff, still a technical tie
items.summary: Datafolha's runoff poll for Folha de S.Paulo, published on Thursday (2,520 interviews on 13–14 October, margin of error 2 points, TSE registration BR-00466/2026), has Flávio Bolsonaro at 47% and Lula at 45%.

items.headline: All 59 PQ MNAs sworn in; cabinet still due 21 October
items.summary: On Thursday 15 October, all 59 Parti Québécois members of Quebec's National Assembly were sworn in at the Red Room in Quebec City, taking an oath of allegiance to the people of Quebec rather than to the King.
items.source: Canadian Press via CityNews Radio-Canada Le Devoir National Post

items.headline: Israel Hayom poll: change bloc 52, right 50; Yashar 24; Winter still below the threshold
items.summary: An Israel Hayom / Kantar poll published on Thursday (551 adults online, 14–15 October, margin of error 4.2 points) puts the change bloc at 52 seats and the right at 50.

items.headline: Lieberman rules out a minority government and Arab or Haredi partners
items.summary: On Thursday Avigdor Lieberman told a conference of the Israel Democracy Institute that Yisrael Beytenu would oppose any minority government and demanded a majority coalition of Zionist parties only.

items.headline: Israel Hayom reports a U.S. push for Netanyahu–Eisenkot unity; Huckabee denies it
items.summary: Israel Hayom on Thursday described a proposed framework in which Likud and Yashar would form a broad government, with Netanyahu serving up to two years then retiring; U.S. Ambassador Mike Huckabee denied any U.S. effort to steer the election.
items.source: Israel Hayom Channel 14 Mike Huckabee on X

items.headline: Colombia withdraws from the Hague Group after opening its Jerusalem embassy
items.summary: Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar announced Colombia's withdrawal as a member and co-chair of the Hague Group, a coalition that sought legal and diplomatic pressure on Israel over Gaza.

items.headline: SpaceXSI releases Grok Voice 3.0; tops Artificial Analysis speech-to-speech ranking
items.summary: On 14 October SpaceXSI released Grok Voice 3.0, its newest speech-to-speech model for the Voice Agent API.

items.headline: SpaceXSI launches The X Subscription, bundling Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium
items.summary: On 12 October SpaceXSI introduced The X Subscription, one plan that includes Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium.

items.headline: Reports: Cursor reviewed whether employee Grok Bot testing sent confidential data toward SpaceXAI training
items.summary: On 15 October TokenPost reported that Cursor staff in late July 2026 reviewed whether use of an internal Grok Bot test tool called Sand could have put confidential customer, supplier or partner information into data shared for SpaceXAI model training.

items.headline: School protests: a mainly high-school movement, now in its fourth week, with about 8,000 people taken into custody
items.summary: A mainly high-school movement over teacher shortages and crowded classes; about 161,500 marched on 13 October by police count; about 8,000 taken into custody, mostly minors; 937 police and 248 pupils injured.
items.source: franceinfo (custody figures) TF1 Info (Lecornu's injury figures) The Guardian Euronews BBC AP CNews (8 October) Human Rights Watch

items.headline: Who backs the protests, what each side says, and how the government has responded
items.summary: Unions and the left back the pupils; the government, LR and the RN blame LFI for fanning violence; Mélenchon denies organizing it.
items.source: Le Monde, 1 October BFMTV, 1 October Human Rights Watch Euronews (grenade suspension) BBC (CGT)

items.headline: Public opinion and possible effect on the 2027 election: support for the pupils, rejection of LFI's role
items.summary: Polls: about 48 to 62 percent back the pupils, but most want the protests to end and most reject LFI's involvement; no clear movement yet in first-round polls.
items.source: Elabe / BFMTV Cluster17 / L'Opinion Ifop / LCI Ipsos Odoxa / Le Figaro Le Dauphiné The Soufan Center Anadolu (RTL poll)

items.headline: Glucksmann wins the left's primary in the first round
items.summary: On 11 October Raphaël Glucksmann, leader of Place publique, won the joint primary of the Socialist Party, Place publique and the Gauche républicaine et socialiste in the first round, with 66.17 percent (79,613 votes).

items.headline: Ifop: Glucksmann ties Philippe; Le Pen at 34 percent
items.summary: In an Ifop-Fiducial poll for LCI and Sud Radio (1,390 people, 12–14 October), published three days after the primary, Glucksmann and Édouard Philippe each have 14 percent in the central scenario, behind Jean-Luc Mélenchon at 16 and far behind Marine Le Pen at 34; Gabriel Attal has 6.
items.source: L'Opinion Public Sénat (Odoxa) Commission des sondages

items.headline: 2027 budget clears its first vote with help from the National Rally
items.summary: On 13 October the National Assembly rejected the Socialists' preliminary motion to reject the 2027 budget, 236 votes to 149; the National Rally voted with the government.

items.headline: Lecornu presents a budget without a majority and hopes for a compromise by December
items.summary: Lecornu presented the 2027 budget to the Council of Ministers on 1 October, as last year without a majority in Parliament.

items.headline: Le Pen would end financial aid to Ukraine after six months
items.summary: Marine Le Pen said on 14 October that, if she is elected, she would keep France's financial aid to Ukraine for six months and then end it, saying that France no longer has the means.

items.headline: Le Pen's appeal to the Court of Cassation moves forward
items.summary: The deadline for the written arguments in Le Pen's appeal to the Court of Cassation passed on 15 October (1 October for the lawyers who joined first).

items.headline: Essayist Natacha Polony declares her candidacy
items.summary: Natacha Polony, the essayist and former editor of Marianne, announced on France Inter on 14 October that she will run, under the slogan "We are France." Her program centers on industrial and energy sovereignty, jobs, schools, public services and the fight against corruption.

items.headline: Polymarket: Le Pen at about 46 percent
items.summary: On Polymarket's market for the winner of the next French presidential election (about $152 million traded), Le Pen stood at about 46 percent on 16 October, followed by Édouard Philippe at about 18.5, David Lisnard and Jean-Luc Mélenchon at about 11.5 each, and Glucksmann at about 4.

items.headline: A citizen-run gallery on East Hanover Street, years in the making, opens its fourth show
items.summary: Hanover Creative Gallery at 219 East Hanover Street, a project its founders began planning in 2019, opened in March 2026 with the textile show 'Fiber Politic' and held its ribbon cutting on 2 April. Its curator, Áine Mickey, is a local organizer who earlier assembled shows at Trenton's BSB Gallery. A new group show, 'Vicious Involution,' runs from 2 to 31 October. NJArts.net wrote that it takes co

items.headline: Meridian Furniture, a private Trenton company, buys 10 acres for a 220,000-square-foot warehouse
items.summary: On 15 September the City Council approved the sale of more than 10 acres of city land at 300 to 366 Enterprise Avenue to Meridian Furniture for $1 million. The company, founded in Trenton more than 20 years ago, will build a warehouse of about 220,000 square feet with its own money. No subsidy has been reported; the city's part was to sell unused land at a price, which returns it to the tax rolls.
items.source: City of Trenton Quadratín Hispano Trenton planning agenda

items.headline: Privately owned Ironhawks hockey team begins play in Trenton on 24 October
items.summary: The Trenton Ironhawks, a new ECHL team, open their first season at CURE Insurance Arena on 24 October against the Adirondack Thunder and will play 36 home games. The team is owned by Pro Hockey Partners, a private group of partners led by Joe Eng. Public element: the arena itself is publicly owned by Mercer County (not independently checked for this item).
items.source: Central Jersey Media Trenton Ironhawks CURE Insurance Arena

items.headline: City puts 28 abandoned buildings into private hands, with priority for buyers who will repair and live in them
items.summary: From 1 to 30 October the city is taking applications from private buyers for 28 city-owned houses and buildings in all four wards. This passes the test of this section because it returns vacant property to private owners rather than spending public money on it; the repairs would be private. Many buildings need major work, and buyers who will live in them receive priority. How many private buyers a
items.source: City of Trenton release, 30 Sep New Jersey Globe

items.headline: Private home buyers are paying more: city reports average sale price up 5.8 percent
items.summary: According to the city, Multiple Listing Service data show the average sale price of a Trenton home rose from about $226,000 in 2025 to about $239,000 so far in 2026. Unconfirmed: this is the city's own reading of the data. Redfin shows recent median sale prices near $250,000, which is consistent with rising private demand but is not the same measure.

items.headline: Maariv poll: blocs tied at 51, Likud falls to 18, Arab parties reach 14
items.summary: A Maariv poll by Lazar Research with Panel4All (700 respondents, 14–15 October, margin of error 3.7 points), published on 16 October, puts Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar at 21 seats and Likud at 18, down two from the previous week.

items.headline: Channel 12 Friday poll: anti-Netanyahu parties 49 percent, Netanyahu bloc 37
items.summary: A Channel 12 poll by Midgam (Mano Geva) for the Friday program Ulpan Shishi, taken on 15 October among 503 respondents (margin of error 4.4 points), found 49 percent support for the parties opposed to Netanyahu, including the Arab parties, against 37 percent for the Netanyahu bloc, including Winter's party.

items.headline: Surplus-vote deadline passes: Ben-Gvir, Winter and Hendel–Zelekha are left without partners
items.summary: The deadline for surplus-vote agreements passed at noon on Friday, 16 October (the law allowed digital filing until the end of the day, so the final list awaits publication by the Central Elections Committee).
items.source: Ynet N12 Madad 120 (missions turnout) Madad 120 (surplus agreements)

items.headline: Polymarket: Eisenkot reaches about 50 percent
items.summary: On Polymarket's market for Israel's next prime minister (about $47 million traded), Gadi Eisenkot stood at about 50 percent on the morning of 17 October, up from about 48 percent on 15 October.

items.headline: Hezbollah admits the seized explosives are its own and demands them back; Rubio says that is 'out of the question'
items.summary: On 15 October the Hezbollah member of parliament Hassan Fadlallah acknowledged that the explosives seized by the Lebanese army on 5 October at the Dahr al-Baidar checkpoint belong to Hezbollah.
items.source: Al Jazeera Middle East Monitor i24NEWS Walla

items.headline: EUSM Lebanon watch: no Israeli reaction yet; the mission is established but not yet launched
items.summary: No new Israeli official or unofficial reaction to the EU Support Mission in Lebanon was found since the last edition, in Hebrew or English media or on X, and no further contributing countries have been named beyond Italy, France and Spain.
items.source: Military Ledger (Hebrew) Council of the EU

items.headline: Two new runoff polls: Flávio Bolsonaro barely ahead, within the margin of error
items.summary: Two polls published on 16 October show the 25 October runoff almost even.

items.headline: Polymarket: Flávio Bolsonaro falls to about 78 percent
items.summary: On Polymarket's Brazil presidential election market (about $185 million traded), Flávio Bolsonaro fell to about 78 percent on 17 October, from about 84 percent on 15 October; Lula rose to about 21.5 percent.

items.headline: Colombian foreign minister ends Israel visit with Herzog; tourist visa exemption restored
items.summary: Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar ended his four-day official visit to Israel on 16 October with a meeting with President Isaac Herzog.

items.headline: SpaceX AI official testifies to the New York City Council on Grok safety
items.summary: On 16 October Gabriela Castillo Madrid, head of government affairs for SpaceX's AI business, testified by video to a New York City Council hearing on AI safety, after the Council threatened to enforce a subpoena.

items.headline: SpaceX will report third-quarter results on 20 October
items.summary: SpaceX will publish its results for the third quarter of 2026 after the market closes on Tuesday, 20 October, and will hold a webcast at 4:30 p.m.

items.headline: Cursor: cloud agents can build shareable canvases; Environments API in beta
items.summary: Cursor's changelog of 16 October says cloud agents can now build interactive canvases and share them by link.

items.headline: Electricity Authority plans a 200-megawatt cap per new data center; decision due Sunday
items.summary: Israel's Electricity Authority plans to limit each new data center to 200 megawatts and to publish the draft for three weeks of public comment, starting on Sunday, 18 October, Calcalist reported on 14 October.
items.source: Calcalist (Ctech) The State of Israel TheMarker

items.headline: China lets Visa prepare a domestic card-clearing business and books its first US soybeans since the summit
items.summary: China's central bank approved on 13 October Visa's application to prepare a domestic bank-card clearing institution; Visa has one year to prepare and cannot yet issue renminbi cards.
items.source: South China Morning Post China Daily Quartz

items.headline: China proposes export controls on 40 technologies, including AI and solar
items.summary: On 16 October China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology proposed adding 40 technologies, in fields including artificial intelligence, biomedicine and solar power, to the catalogue of technologies whose export is restricted: 14 would be banned and 26 would need a license.
items.source: Caixin Global China Daily Ministry of Commerce (Chinese)

items.headline: Burnham rules out a second Scottish independence referendum while he is prime minister
items.summary: On his first major visit to Scotland as prime minister, in Motherwell on 16 October, Andy Burnham ruled out a second independence referendum during his premiership; Downing Street sources said this applies to his whole time as leader.

items.headline: Greenland's parliament votes to prepare a ban on deep-sea mining until 2029
items.summary: On 15 October Greenland's parliament, Inatsisartut, unanimously adopted a resolution telling the government to draft a temporary ban on deep-sea mining and exploration until 31 December 2029, which could be extended two years at a time.

items.headline: St-Pierre Plamondon: fix Quebec first, then talk of independence
items.summary: At the swearing-in of the Parti Québécois's 59 members of the National Assembly on 15 October, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon closed with 'Vive le Québec libre' but said that before talking about independence the PQ must 'get Quebec back on the rails' and regain voters' confidence, the Montreal Gazette reported.

items.headline: A local developer's graffiti museum plans a five-story home on East State Street
items.summary: The American Graffiti Museum, a nonprofit founded in 2021 by the Trenton native Daniel R.
items.source: Princeton Info / Trenton Downtowner NJEDA (grant list) Trenton Journal

items.headline: OpinionWay: Glucksmann gains after the primary, Philippe at his lowest, Le Pen at 35 to 37
items.summary: Two OpinionWay polls taken on 13 and 14 October, after the left's primary (978 registered voters in a sample of 1,043), were published on 15 October.
items.source: OpinionWay (Les Echos) OpinionWay report (PDF) OpinionWay for CNEWS (PDF) Sud Ouest

items.headline: Lecornu: the school movement has become 'urban violence'; it weakens as the holidays begin
items.summary: On 15 October Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said that the movement 'no longer looks like a high-school movement' but like 'a movement of urban violence,' with violence increasing in Paris, Créteil and Lyon.
items.source: Le Parisien BFMTV franceinfo Ouest-France DNA

items.headline: Saturday 17 October: a 'convergence' day against the cost of living, with bans in central Paris
items.summary: Pupils, so-called students, former gilets jaunes, climate activists, the CGT-led union alliance and the Confédération paysanne have called for a joint day of protest against the cost of living on Saturday, 17 October; the main farmers' unions, the FNSEA and the Coordination rurale, are not taking part.

items.headline: Opinion and analysis: 69 percent approve of the 17 October protest; an essayist doubts a repeat of 2018
items.summary: An Elabe poll for BFMTV (1,506 people, 14–16 October) finds that 69 percent of the French approve of the mobilization against the cost of living (36 percent support it and 33 percent feel sympathy; 14 percent are indifferent, 10 percent opposed and 7 percent hostile).
items.source: BFMTV (Elabe) Le Parisien TF1 Info RTL

items.headline: Protest day: clashes in Paris, Lyon, Bordeaux, Marseille and Lille; 272 arrests by 3 p.m.
items.summary: The 17 October day of protest against the cost of living brought tens of thousands into the streets and violent clashes in several cities.
items.source: Europe 1 / AFP live BFMTV France 24 / AFP (Paris police details) France 24 live, with AP (car and kiosk)

items.headline: Ipespe poll: Flávio 48, Lula 46; first runoff debate on Sunday
items.summary: A third poll this week shows the runoff within the margin of error, with the gap narrowing.
items.source: Veja CNN Brasil BBC News Brasil

items.headline: Elabe: Philippe, Glucksmann and Mélenchon level at about 15 to 16 percent behind Le Pen
items.summary: An Elabe poll for BFMTV and La Tribune Dimanche, taken online from 14 to 16 October among 1,701 people (1,533 registered voters) and published on 17 October, puts Marine Le Pen at 31 to 33.5 percent in the first round, down 1 to 1.5 points since Elabe's August poll.

items.headline: 17 October final count: 550,000 marchers by police count, 1,200 arrests, 150 police injured, Limoges town hall burned
items.summary: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 550,000 people marched in about 110 cities on 17 October, 110,000 of them in Paris; the organizers claimed 800,000.
items.source: BFMTV (550,000) BFMTV (1,200 arrests) 20 Minutes Europe 1 TF1info (Saint-Étienne) RFI / AFP (Limoges) France 24 (looting)

items.headline: Lecornu tells LFI to "choose its side"; Le Pen blames the far left; Mélenchon blames the government
items.summary: After the violence of 17 October Lecornu told La France insoumise that it was "time to choose your side," the Republic and the police or "the rioters," and spoke of a "point of no return."
items.source: 20 Minutes (Lecornu–Mélenchon) BFMTV (Le Pen, Mélenchon) Le Monde (Macron) Le Parisien (reactions) Paris Match (analysis) Assemblée nationale (budget calendar)

items.headline: Netanyahu: "We're tied"; Bennett and Liberman name their first laws; Eisenkot gives an 18-month Gaza pledge
items.summary: Ten days before the 27 October election, Prime Minister Netanyahu told i24NEWS on 17 October that the race is "tied" and urged his voters to turn out, warning that Iran, Hezbollah and Hamas would try to interfere, including by "creating security incidents."
items.source: Times of Israel (Bennett, Liberman) Times of Israel (Netanyahu) Ynetnews Eisenkot on X Globes (poll average) Polymarket

items.headline: Lebanon will press for a halt to Israeli strikes at the Tampa talks on 20 October; Qatar pledges a solar plant
items.summary: The Lebanese presidency said on 17 October that its military delegation will demand a halt to Israeli attacks at the US–Lebanon–Israel military meeting at US Central Command in Tampa on 20 October.
items.source: Al-Monitor / Reuters Ynetnews Al Jazeera (Qatar) Qatar Foreign Ministry

items.headline: PoderData ties the runoff at 50–50; Gerp has Flávio 52 to 48; Polymarket back near 80 percent
items.summary: Two more runoff polls were published on 16 October: PoderData/Aya (3,000 telephone interviews, 13–15 October, margin 1.8 points) has Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro tied at 50 percent of valid votes.
items.source: CNN Brasil (PoderData) Poder360 (Gerp) CNN Brasil (Gerp) Poder360 (poll summary) Polymarket

items.headline: Amazon blocks Grok Bot orders; Musk replies, "Maybe we should start a competitor to Amazon"
items.summary: Amazon is blocking orders placed by Grok Bot, as it does with other AI shopping agents, including Meta's Muse.

items.headline: Texas Monthly: state commission planned a closed-door talk on selling Boca Chica State Park; SpaceX named as buyer (unconfirmed)
items.summary: Texas Monthly reported on 16 October that the Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission had planned a closed-door discussion on 5 November about selling the 1,300-acre Boca Chica State Park next to SpaceX's Starbase.

items.headline: Swinney: "The referendum campaign on Scottish independence has already begun"
items.summary: In his speech to the SNP conference in Aberdeen on 17 October, First Minister John Swinney said the independence referendum campaign "has already begun" and launched a "Choose Scotland" campaign; his spokesman said it starts with £100,000.
items.source: The Herald The National SNP (speech text)

items.headline: Council moves to buy the empty Lafayette Yard hotel with a $4 million state grant and hand it to a private redeveloper for $1
items.summary: Trenton City Council voted on 6 October to apply for a $4 million New Jersey Economic Development Authority grant to buy the former Lafayette Yard Marriott at 1 West Lafayette Street, the city's only downtown hotel, empty since the state closed it for safety violations in 2017.
items.source: Trentonian Central Jersey Media NJ.com Trenton Journal (lawsuit background)

items.headline: Israel's ambassador: Colombia is considering joining the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance
items.summary: Israel's ambassador to Colombia, Vivian Aisen, told The Media Line that Foreign Ministers Gideon Sa'ar and Omar Bula discussed a possible Colombian application to the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance during Bula's visit to Jerusalem.

items.headline: Evening: Trump gives Netanyahu his 'Complete and Total Endorsement'; Eisenkot falls to about 47 percent on Polymarket
items.summary: In a Truth Social post on Sunday afternoon addressed 'To the Great People of Israel,' President Trump called Netanyahu a 'Great Warrior Prime Minister' and wrote: 'Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election.' He tied the endorsement to Iran, warned that unless Iran changes course 'we will soon finish the job,'

items.headline: Evening: Netanyahu says Ben-Gvir will 'unequivocally' be in his next government; Ben-Gvir says Netanyahu's office told European states the opposite
items.summary: Asked by reporters on Sunday whether the broad government he wants after the election would include Ben-Gvir's party, Netanyahu answered 'unequivocally' and said his wish to keep the Defense and National Security ministries in Likud is no sign of a different coalition: 'there is no doubt we will make the same coalition' (Arutz 7).

items.headline: Evening: Aoun asks France's Barrot for help against a security vacuum in the south when UNIFIL leaves
items.summary: President Joseph Aoun told visiting French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot in Baabda on Sunday that Lebanon still wants UNIFIL's mandate extended, but that if this is impossible it 'welcomes any arrangement that ensures an international presence in the south, prevents a vacuum, and avoids placing the Lebanese Army in direct contact with the Israeli army' (Naharnet; the Times of Israel reported t

items.headline: Evening: the first runoff debate is tonight on Band; poll averages show a technical tie with Lula gaining
items.summary: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro meet in their first runoff debate on Band at 8 p.m.

items.headline: Evening: the 17 October toll rises to more than 2,000 arrests and more than 600 police, gendarmes and firefighters injured; a marcher dies after collapsing in Paris
items.summary: At midday on Sunday Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez raised the count to more than 2,000 arrests across France and more than 600 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters injured, figures he called provisional (BFMTV; franceinfo).
items.source: BFMTV franceinfo France 24 / AFP TF1 Info (death) Times of Israel, French edition (synagogue)

items.headline: Evening: new clashes and looting at Place de la République; Macron will speak at 8 p.m.; mayors to rally at town halls on Monday
items.summary: On Sunday afternoon an undeclared gathering at Place de la République in Paris turned into clashes between several hundred people and the police, and looting resumed nearby; the police sent in the CRS 8 riot unit (CNews; BFMTV).
items.source: CNews live BFMTV live France 24 / AFP

items.headline: Evening: Musk says the SpaceX–Nvidia 'Star Mind' computer will reach volume production next year
items.summary: Elon Musk wrote on X on 15 October that the 'Star Mind' computer being co-engineered by SpaceX and Nvidia is 'far better than almost anyone expects and will reach volume production next year,' and Nvidia's Jensen Huang said on the BG2 podcast that the two engineering teams are designing a new server meant to put data centers in space (Benzinga, carried by Yahoo Finance on 17 October).

items.headline: Three Sunday polls: Kan has Yashar 23 and Likud 21; i24NEWS has Likud 25; Channel 14 has Netanyahu's bloc at exactly 61
items.summary: Three seat polls published on Sunday evening, 18 October, nine days before the vote, point in different directions.
items.source: Kan News Haaretz i24NEWS (Hebrew) Channel 14 Israel National News Polymarket

items.headline: Netanyahu presents a new security doctrine: 'The regime must fall, and I will bring it down'; Eisenkot calls it 'two hollow pages'
items.summary: On Sunday Netanyahu held a two-hour security briefing for Israeli reporters at his Jerusalem office, his first such in-person briefing since 7 October 2023; several outlets boycotted it (Times of Israel).

items.headline: Former chief rabbi Yitzhak Yosef rules it forbidden to vote for Otzma Yehudit; IDF weighs a leave freeze on election day
items.summary: Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef, the former Sephardi chief rabbi and a member of Shas's Council of Torah Sages, published a letter on Sunday ruling that it is forbidden under Jewish law to vote for Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit, because Ben-Gvir goes up to the Temple Mount and encourages others to do so; he wrote that whoever votes for the party carries the sin (Arutz 7; Times of Israel).
items.source: Arutz 7 The Times of Israel (live blog, 18 October) N12 The Times of Israel

items.headline: Before the Tampa talks: Lebanon's demands, Netanyahu's verdict on the army's pilot zones, and a Hezbollah defense of arms transfers
items.summary: The US–Lebanon–Israel military meeting at US Central Command in Tampa is set for Tuesday, 20 October.
items.source: Israel Hayom The Times of Israel L'Orient Today Lebanon Times

items.headline: EUSM Lebanon watch: Ireland's government moves to take part; still no Israeli reaction
items.summary: Ireland's government has said it wants to contribute to the EU Support Mission in Lebanon.

items.headline: Electricity Authority caps each new data center at 200 megawatts; reports differ on the national ceiling
items.summary: The plenum of Israel's Electricity Authority decided on Sunday evening, 18 October, that each new data center may connect to the grid at no more than 200 megawatts, and that developers must post guarantees of NIS 2 million per megawatt, or NIS 400 million for a full 200-megawatt site, to keep out speculative applications (Globes; TheMarker).

items.headline: Macron speaks of "anger and shame," promises the looters will pay, but declares no state of emergency and offers no new measures
items.summary: President Macron addressed the nation for about nine minutes at 8 p.m. Paris time on 18 October (9 p.m. in Israel), saying, "We all feel anger and shame tonight."
items.source: Élysée: address to the French people, 18 Oct franceinfo France 24 Nord Littoral

items.headline: Bardella calls the address "lamentable," Retailleau asks again for a state of emergency, Philippe wants decisions; LFI calls it "irresponsible"
items.summary: Candidates on the right and left criticized the address.
items.source: BFMTV TF1 Info Le Figaro (live) Bruno Retailleau on X Édouard Philippe on X Jean-Luc Mélenchon on X

items.headline: Final 17 October toll: 2,397 arrests and 997 police and gendarmes injured; more looting in Paris on Sunday night; curfew for minors in Guadeloupe
items.summary: The Interior Ministry's consolidated count for 17 October is 2,397 arrests and 997 police officers and gendarmes injured, seven of them seriously (BFMTV; RFI), up from the provisional 2,000 arrests and 600 injured given at midday on Sunday.
items.source: BFMTV RFI 20 Minutes / AFP Le Figaro / AFP: Guadeloupe France-Antilles Outre-mer La 1ère France 3 Grand Est: Mulhouse RTL: Mulhouse Le Figaro (live)

items.summary: Frédéric Dabi, director general of Ifop, told AFP on 18 October that the risk of a flare-up six months before a presidential election is "totally unprecedented" under the Fifth Republic; he said the chaos of 17 October could "strengthen Marine Le Pen's first-round electoral base" and make it harder for Jean-Luc Mélenchon to reach the runoff, but urged caution about the effect at the polls (Sud Oue
items.source: Sud Ouest / AFP Midi Libre Polymarket Le Figaro (live) Assemblée nationale: budget calendar

items.headline: First runoff debate: Lula and Flávio trade corruption charges; Flávio admits his father's government fell short on health
items.summary: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro traded accusations in their first runoff debate, on Band on the evening of 18 October (it began about 15 minutes late and ended about 10:15 p.m. Brasília time, 4:15 a.m. Monday in Israel).
items.source: Exame O Globo O Globo: Míriam Leitão Band CartaCapital Valor Polymarket

items.headline: Health-tech startup MyMonitor.AI moves its headquarters from Philadelphia to downtown Trenton
items.summary: MyMonitor.AI, a health-care artificial intelligence startup, has moved its headquarters from Philadelphia to Suite 202 at 1 West State Street in downtown Trenton; Mayor Reed Gusciora joined founder and chief executive Charles Mbata for a ribbon cutting on 13 October (Trenton Journal, from a city release; Quadratín).
items.source: Trenton Journal Quadratín Nueva Jersey Community News MyMonitor.AI

items.headline: Grok Bot update: company says computer tasks finish three times faster; The Grid Fin reports X Chat access and new finance connectors
items.summary: The Grok Bot account announced on X on 16 October an update to "quality, polish, and speed": it says computer tasks now finish three times sooner on average and other replies arrive in less than half the time, chat cards have a cleaner design, voice calls are faster and better at remembering past conversations, email supports plus aliases for routines, tagging @bot in an X post starts a task, and
items.source: Grok Bot on X Grok Bot on X: speed The Grid Fin

items.headline: Before Tuesday's results, analysts expect SpaceX's first quarterly profit as a listed company
items.summary: SpaceX reports third-quarter results after the market closes on Tuesday, 20 October, with an audio webcast at 4:30 p.m. New York time (11:30 p.m. in Israel); it is the first report to include Cursor, bought in August (TECHi).

items.headline: Andreessen posts an original film comment on X: "At long last, movies are back"
items.summary: On 18 October 2026 at 8:01 a.m. Israel time, Marc Andreessen wrote on X: "YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING, PRIMETIME, and DIGGER make 2026 the best year for film since 2015 (SICARIO, EX MACHINA, and MAD MAX: FURY ROAD). At long last, movies are back."

items.headline: Gantz pulls Blue and White out of the race; Sa'ar and Smotrich press Winter to follow, and he refuses
items.summary: Benny Gantz announced on Monday afternoon, 19 October, that his Blue and White party will not run in the 27 October election, reversing his statement a week earlier that he would stay in the race 'no matter what' (Ynet; Israel Hayom; Jerusalem Post).
items.source: Ynet Israel Hayom Jerusalem Post Channel 14 Times of Israel

items.headline: Three Monday polls: Channel 12 has Eisenkot's bloc 55–51; Channel 13 has it 51–50; Channel 14 gives the right 62
items.summary: Three seat polls published on Monday evening, 19 October, eight days before the vote, again disagree.
items.source: Haaretz Times of Israel Walla Maariv Channel 14 Ice Polymarket

items.headline: Channel 12: Netanyahu aide Urich told police he kept working for Qatar into 2024; Bennett calls it treason
items.summary: Channel 12 reported on Monday evening, citing transcripts of his questioning by the police unit Lahav 433, that Netanyahu's adviser Jonatan Urich admitted he kept working with Qatari clients until at least mid-2024, months after the 7 October 2023 attack, and was paid hundreds of thousands of shekels (Channel 12; Ynet; Times of Israel).

items.headline: Tampa talks open Tuesday; Lebanon says it will refuse direct army-to-army coordination with Israel
items.summary: Lebanese and Israeli military delegations meet on Tuesday and Wednesday, 20 and 21 October, at US Central Command in Tampa, with US Marine Corps Major General Joseph Clearfield leading the American side, according to official Lebanese sources quoted by LBCI and Naharnet; earlier reports had said the talks would run to 22 October.
items.source: The National L'Orient Today LBCI Naharnet MTV Lebanon (X)

items.headline: Beirut: army steps up patrols after Hezbollah supporters block a police raid; Aoun orders a ban on armed demonstrations
items.summary: The Lebanese army has increased patrols and set up temporary checkpoints in Beirut and its southern suburbs after a rise in tension with Hezbollah supporters (The National; L'Orient Today).

items.headline: Data center rules: about 1,300 new megawatts until 2030, NIS 2 million guarantees, and a separate plan to give sites land without tenders
items.summary: Fuller reports on the Electricity Authority's 18 October decision explain the difference between earlier accounts.

items.headline: SCMP: US and Chinese negotiators push for investment deals before the November Trump–Xi meeting in Shenzhen; China adds export controls on drones and tunnel borers
items.summary: The South China Morning Post reported on 20 October, citing several unnamed sources, that US and Chinese negotiators have made 'considerable progress' on setting up a joint Board of Investment ahead of Trump and Xi's planned meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen in November, modeled on the Board of Trade led by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Vice Premier
items.source: South China Morning Post Anadolu Agency Peter's World China Ministry of Commerce (Chinese)

items.headline: EU presents its Arctic strategy today, with a secure undersea cable to Greenland; Nuuk's vote on the US defense agreement is set for 3 November
items.summary: The European Commission is due to present a new Arctic strategy on Tuesday, 20 October, and drafts seen by Euronews and AFP say the EU will connect Greenland to Europe with a 'sovereign and secure submarine cable' and work on a longer-term cable from Europe through Greenland and Canada to Japan (Euronews also names South Korea).

items.headline: BDRC releases Yigdzin, a free open model for reading Tibetan texts
items.summary: The Buddhist Digital Resource Center (BDRC) in Boston has released Yigdzin, an open OCR model that converts scanned Tibetan pages into searchable text, announced on 16 October and not reported here before.
items.source: Buddhist Digital Resource Center Hugging Face (BDRC model card)

items.headline: Nuñez offers to resign and Macron refuses; first local curfews in Paris, Lyon, Nice, the Lille area and Bordeaux
items.summary: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez offered his resignation after Macron's address on the evening of 18 October, and the Élysée said on Monday morning that the president refused it because of 'the need for continuous command of the police,' while asking for 'new methods of action' against rioters (franceinfo; BFMTV; Le Parisien).

items.summary: A YouGov poll for Le HuffPost, taken online from 12 to 15 October among 1,094 adults (976 registered voters) and published on 18 October, puts Marine Le Pen at 35 to 37 percent in the first round.
items.source: Le HuffPost Commission des sondages: YouGov notice PollingForecast: second round Polymarket

items.headline: Budget: the Assembly suspends the vote on the revenue part and moves to the social security budget; minister says the debate has added €10 billion to the deficit
items.summary: The solemn vote on the first (revenue) part of the 2027 state budget, planned for Tuesday 20 October, has been postponed: the National Assembly stopped debating it at midnight on Monday with more than 2,600 amendments still to examine, and takes up the social security budget from Tuesday afternoon, as the constitutional deadlines require.

items.headline: Liberal MNAs sworn in, all to the people of Quebec; PQ cabinet to be sworn in on Wednesday without the lieutenant governor
items.summary: The 40 Liberal members of the National Assembly were sworn in at the Red Room on 19 October; all of them took only the oath to the people of Quebec, not the optional oath to the King, and about half took it in both French and English (Canadian Press via L'actualité).
items.source: L'actualité (Canadian Press) Le Devoir TVA Nouvelles

items.headline: SpaceX reports third-quarter results today after the market closes; analysts expect revenue of about $12.7 billion
items.summary: SpaceX's third-quarter results had not been released by early 20 October; they are due after the New York market closes on Tuesday, with a webcast at 4:30 p.m. Eastern time (11:30 p.m. in Israel).
items.source: Reuters via CNBC-TV18 Yahoo Finance SpaceX investor relations

items.headline: Musk pledges one of his SpaceX shares to every American child next year
items.summary: Elon Musk wrote on X on 19 October that next year he will give one of his SpaceX shares to every child in the United States, adding, 'This will be the first of many'; he gave no details on eligibility or how the shares would be distributed.
items.source: CNBC Forbes The Wall Street Journal

items.headline: Military court summons two Hezbollah officials over a seized explosives shipment
items.summary: Claude Ghanem, the government commissioner to Lebanon's military court, on 20 October summoned two Hezbollah officials known as 'Sajed' and 'Dulfiqar' over the explosives shipment that army intelligence seized at Dahr al-Baidar, and security agencies are trying to locate them (MTV; Naharnet; Times of Israel).
items.source: Naharnet MTV Lebanon Times of Israel

items.headline: First poll after the riots: Ifop has Le Pen at 34 to 38 percent, Mélenchon second and Philippe out in every scenario
items.summary: An Ifop-Fiducial poll for LCI, Le Figaro and Sud Radio, taken online from the evening of 17 October to 19 October among 1,928 registered voters and published on 20 October, is the first measured after the 17 October violence.
items.source: Ifop: wave 7 results (PDF) Le Figaro TF1 Info Le Parisien Polymarket

items.headline: Soldiers to guard sites so police are free for Saturday; curfews spread to Marseille and Bordeaux; 700 brought before judges
items.summary: Prime Minister Lecornu promised a 'massive' security operation for Saturday, 24 October, when student unions and the gilets jaunes plan new protests, and Interior Minister Nuñez told parliament that Operation Sentinelle soldiers will take over static guard duties to free police officers; he is also considering a ban on undeclared demonstrations (Euronews; France 24).

items.headline: Real Time Big Data has Flávio ahead 48 to 45; Polymarket rises back to about 81 percent; Quaest and Datafolha due Wednesday and Thursday
items.summary: A Real Time Big Data poll published on 20 October (2,000 voters, 15–19 October, margin of error 2 points, registered with the electoral court as BR-02952/2026) puts Flávio Bolsonaro at 48 percent and Lula at 45, or 52 to 48 in valid votes (Brasil de Fato).

items.headline: St-Pierre Plamondon's cabinet is sworn in today: about 20 ministers, a minister for the independence process, and Paradis as chief negotiator
items.summary: The Parti Québécois cabinet is sworn in on Wednesday, 21 October, at 1:30 p.m. Quebec time (8:30 p.m. Israel time), without the lieutenant governor, Manon Jeannotte, who was not invited and will sign the appointment acts in her office (Le Devoir; Radio-Canada).

items.headline: EU adopts its Arctic strategy: a direct cable from Greenland to Europe, €200 million for Greenland, and shared icebreakers
items.summary: The European Commission and High Representative Kaja Kallas adopted 'Europe's Northern Neighbourhood – A New Strategy for the Arctic' on 20 October, with four priorities: security and resilience, climate, prosperity, and people (European Commission; EEAS).
items.source: European Commission: digital strategy European Commission EEAS: Kallas remarks KNR

items.headline: SpaceX's third quarter: revenue up 161 percent to $14.6 billion and a $4.4 billion profit, driven by AI; Cursor added $608 million

items.source: SEC: SpaceX Q3 2026 release Reuters via NBC News Reuters via Investing.com AP Wall Street Journal

items.headline: Musk: SpaceX and Tesla have set up independent committees to study a merger; shares rise after hours
items.summary: On the earnings call Musk said SpaceX and Tesla have each formed a special committee of independent directors to explore a merger; he called it 'a good idea' but said it is not certain, no terms are agreed, and a deal would need a majority of all outstanding Tesla shares, describing the process as 'an odd kabuki dance' (Yahoo Finance; BBC; Reuters).
items.source: Yahoo Finance BBC Reuters via NBC News

items.headline: City breaks ground on the restoration of the Carver Center, the 1922 hall where Ella Fitzgerald and Duke Ellington played
items.summary: The City of Trenton broke ground on 20 October on the first phase of restoring the Carver Center at 40 Fowler Street: a contract of about $2.53 million for the roof and exterior, part of a restoration expected to cost about $8 million (Trenton Journal, from a city release; InsiderNJ).

items.summary: The US-mediated military talks between Israel and Lebanon at Central Command in Tampa closed on 22 October, after a third day, without agreement and without a date for a next round (Ynet; The New Arab).

items.summary: Prime Minister Lecornu received representatives of 28 parties at Matignon on 22 October to discuss public order.

items.headline: OpinionWay after the riots: Le Pen 36, Mélenchon 16, Glucksmann 13, Philippe 12; Lisnard passes Attal
items.summary: OpinionWay for CNews and Europe 1 (21–22 October, 973 registered voters) has Marine Le Pen at 36 percent in the first round (up 1), Jean-Luc Mélenchon 16 (up 1), Raphaël Glucksmann 13, Édouard Philippe 12, David Lisnard 6 (up 2), Bruno Retailleau 6, Gabriel Attal 4 (down 2) and Éric Zemmour 4, with 13 percent undecided.

items.headline: Signal 22, the volunteer canteen that feeds Trenton firefighters and police at emergencies, marks 85 years
items.summary: The Signal 22 Association, a volunteer group that brings food and drinks to firefighters and police at fires and other long emergencies, marked its 85th anniversary on 17 October.

items.summary: The Trenton Journal profiled Alex Bethea, a former Trenton teacher and City Council president who co-founded the Trenton Youth Wrestling & Learning Center, which pairs wrestling with tutoring and mentoring for city children.

items.headline: Orléans locked down for the RN congress: about 3,000 police, 20,000 to 30,000 counter-marchers on Saturday, and Le Pen's campaign launch on Sunday
items.summary: The National Rally's congress opens in Orléans on Saturday, 24 October. About 3,000 police and gendarmes are deployed around two security zones, and the authorities expect 20,000 to 30,000 opponents at an authorized march called by the CGT and left-wing figures (RFI).

items.headline: St-Pierre Plamondon's first measure as premier: $28 million more for homelessness, for 1,000 new shelter and warming-center places
items.summary: On 23 October Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, who also holds the homelessness file, announced $28 million in emergency funding on top of $18 million already allocated, for a total of $46 million and about 1,000 new places in shelters and warming centers this winter.

items.headline: Danish parliament schedules the Greenland–US defense agreement: debate on 12 November, final vote on 19 November
items.summary: Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen presented the new Denmark–Greenland–US security and defense agreement to the Folketing on 22 October as a resolution; the first reading is on 12 November and the final vote on 19 November (Ritzau).
items.source: Copenhagen Post (Ritzau), 23 Oct Ritzau Danish News

items.headline: SCMP: US and Chinese teams work on an AI incident framework as a possible result of the Shenzhen meeting
items.summary: The South China Morning Post reported on 23 October, citing three unnamed sources, that US and Chinese technical teams are in regular talks to give substance to September's plan for an AI incident channel and an AI dialogue, aiming for a basic crisis framework by the Trump–Xi meeting at APEC in Shenzhen in November.
items.source: South China Morning Post via The Star, 23 Oct

items.summary: MLex reports that Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones is considering legal action against xAI over Grok's creation of sexualized images; no complaint has been filed.

items.summary: Brazil votes today, Sunday 25 October. The final polls, published Saturday, all show Flávio Bolsonaro slightly ahead of Lula, mostly within the margin of error.

items.source: RFI, 24 Oct Europe 1 France 3 Centre-Val de Loire

items.headline: St-Pierre Plamondon will skip Monday's first Council of the Federation meeting with Indigenous chiefs in 21 years

items.source: Le Devoir, 24 Oct Le Quotidien, 24 Oct

items.summary: Helen McEntee told RTÉ's This Week on 25 October that Irish troops should be able to take part in "both"; this needs a change to Ireland's "Triple Lock" rule, which she wants passed by the end of the year.

items.summary: Arutz 7 reported that two security men living in Samaria, a community's military security coordinator and a security officer, were arrested at five in the morning on suspicion of involvement in violence against Palestinians near Aqraba about a month ago; they were barred from meeting a lawyer, and a gag order covers the case. items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that one of the shepherds attacked on Saturday near the Kerem Binyamin farm by Ateret went to hospital that night, where examinations found a broken finger and a probable sprain in the leg. items.headline: Regavim: long-dead people are counted in Palestinian population censuses
items.summary: Regavim published an interview given to Channel 14 by Roi Drucker, its coordinator for Judea and Samaria, on the contradictory and unclear figures for the Palestinian population there. Regavim summarised the finding by saying that in the Palestinian Authority people who died long ago are counted in the censuses. The interview also explains why the true size of that population matters to Israel.

items.summary: Olam Katan reported that Supreme Court President Yitzhak Amit and Justices Alex Stein and Khaled Kabub ordered the state to set out a timetable for the steps that would let residents return to the Jenin, Tulkarm and Nur Shams camps, and to examine whether those steps can be accelerated. items.summary: On 10 October hundreds of Arabs from Deir Abu Mash'al, with foreign and far-left activists, some of them masked and carrying clubs, came up towards Givat Tidhar in Wadi Zarqa, western Binyamin, under the pretext of picking olives. items.summary: The IDF Binyamin Brigade and the Border Police of Judea and Samaria completed a week-long operation in five villages, searching more than 600 locations, seizing weapons and incitement material, and arresting wanted men, among them suspects in the transfer of terror funds. items.summary: Lea Ziv-Parag, the widow of Yaakov Parag, who was murdered in December 1988 while guarding the lands of Har Bracha, has written to the head of Central Command, Major General Avi Bluth, asking the army to remove a monument to his murderer, Hamdan al-Najjar, which the family says stands near the place of the murder. items.summary: Peace Now reported that the head of Central Command has signed the harvest orders for 2026: Palestinians may enter about 88,300 dunams of olive groves only with prior coordination with the IDF, about 30 percent more than the 68,800 dunams of 2025 (a dunam is 1,000 square metres). items.headline: Attacks on Israelis under cover of the olive harvest in Samaria and Binyamin
items.summary: Olam Katan reported that on the morning of 9 October Arabs from Zeita waited in an olive grove in the Gush Kana area, between Yitzhar and Emanuel, and stoned the car of Israeli hikers; the windscreen was damaged and no one was hurt. The same morning a Samaria resident on an all-terrain vehicle was rammed and lightly injured near Tapuah, and a Jew was lightly injured in the face by stones near Jama

items.headline: Hikers remove a monument to the murderer of Rabbi Nehemia Lavi and Aharon Bennett
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that hikers of the Chargavim group, touring western Binyamin on 9 October, found a monument in Surda to Muhannad Halabi, who murdered Rabbi Nehemia Lavi and Aharon Bennett in Jerusalem in October 2015, and removed it. Ynet, citing local Palestinian sources, described the same events as an attack by armed settlers who threw stones, fired in the air and damaged a monument. The

items.headline: Wallerstein Road: the IDF has begun preparations to reopen Route 463
items.summary: In an exclusive interview with Olam Katan, published on 8 October, Israel Ganz, head of the Binyamin Regional Council and of the Yesha Council, said that Wallerstein Road (Route 463) is joining the Ma'ozim axis plan and that the IDF has begun work toward its official opening to Israeli traffic. items.summary: On the evening of 8 October residents of Kedumim, in Samaria, heard prolonged heavy gunfire from the Arab village of Kafr Qadum, a few hundred metres away, and the security department called out the community’s forces and the IDF. items.summary: Hakol Hayehudi reported that the Palestinian Authority regularly sends members of its security forces, often in civilian clothes, to olive harvests in Area C and next to Jewish communities, under the name of “protection from settlers”; the director-general of the Palestinian police, Major-General Alam al-Saqa, has ordered higher readiness for the season. items.headline: Attacks on shepherds in Binyamin rise sharply; farmers receive body cameras
items.summary: The Binyamin Regional Council has begun to give body cameras to farmers after a sharp rise in incidents at the start of the olive harvest. By the council’s figures, reports of incidents near farms rose from about 23 to about 48 in the first week of the harvest, attacks on shepherds rose from three to eleven, and more than 140 attacks on shepherds have been recorded since the start of the year. items.headline: New community of Goder in the northern Jordan Valley to be inaugurated on 14 October
items.summary: The new community of Goder, in the northern Jordan Valley, will be formally inaugurated on Wednesday, 14 October. Twelve families already live there, the first of whom arrived about two months ago, and 400 more housing units are planned. The cabinet approved the community on Jerusalem Day 2025; it stands on the site of a former paratrooper base at a junction on Route 5799 between Tubas and Maskiyo

items.headline: First tent put up again at Netzach Shmuel after the demolition
items.summary: After the Civil Administration and the Border Police demolished the hilltop community of Netzach Shmuel, near Adei Ad in Binyamin, the young men who live there returned to the same hill. They have put up the first tent again.

items.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz said this week that the IDF is preparing as never before for a “turning of the barrels”, in which the forces of the Palestinian Authority would turn their weapons on Israelis. “If anyone dares to turn weapons against us, what we did in Gaza and Lebanon will come to Judea and Samaria,” he said, adding that Israel would answer with an all-out campaign. items.headline: Stones near Yitzhar and a firebomb at a bus from al-Fawwar
items.summary: Hatzalah Judea and Samaria reported that at 20:11 on 7 October Arabs threw stones at vehicles between the Yitzhar interchange and the small Yitzhar junction. At 20:42 Arabs from al-Fawwar, in the Hebron hills, threw a firebomb at a bus; it burned at the side of the road. No one was hurt in either attack.
items.source: Hatzalah Judea and Samaria, via Yisrael Medad (X)

items.headline: Nine Jews detained near Susya and Sinia; residents report police violence
items.summary: The police said that Border Police detained seven suspects near Susya, in the southern Hebron hills, over what they called extreme violence, and two residents of Samaria after a reported assault near the village of Sinia. items.summary: Alongside the demolition of the house of the murderer of Netanel Shukron, forces of the IDF, the Shin Bet and the police opened broad brigade operations across Judea and Samaria. items.summary: IDF forces began a broad operation to demolish dozens of monuments glorifying terrorists, among them a central monument in Nablus and one in Ya'bad to a man convicted in the murder of Avner Maimon in 2003. items.summary: A bipartisan delegation of state legislators from Florida, Illinois, Texas, Indiana, Missouri and Alabama visited northern Samaria as guests of Yossi Dagan, head of the Samaria Regional Council. They saw Peduel, the new community of Eival founded this summer, the altar of Joshua on Mount Eival and the lookout above Joseph’s Tomb. items.headline: Shin Bet chief warns of military-type organisation among the Negev Bedouin
items.summary: David Zini, head of the Shin Bet, told the security cabinet of “very worrying” organisation in the unrecognised Bedouin settlements of the Negev, including infrastructure of a military character. He said that attempts have been identified to set up frameworks resembling military battalions. He also warned of ties between residents and terror organisations, Hamas among them.

items.headline: Central Command adopts the doctrine of “the community as a fortress”
items.summary: The IDF stated that Central Command has adopted the doctrine of “the community as a fortress”, with more observation, intelligence, weapons and security components inside the communities, and that all army camps in Judea and Samaria are being turned into fortified posts. items.summary: Residents of Beit Hogla, in the Jordan Valley, are moving on to establish a new community named Elisha on the outskirts of Jericho. Azriel Pikar, one of the four founding families of Beit Hogla almost eleven years ago, said that Beit Hogla now has about sixty families. items.summary: WAFA's Hebrew service reported on 6 October, citing the Palestinian Authority's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, that the IDF has issued seizure order No. 33/26 for 741 square metres in the al-Jabriyat neighbourhood of Jenin, in Area A. items.headline: Paving begins on the Homesh–Sa-Nur road in northern Samaria
items.summary: Arutz 7 reported on 6 October that, after six months of earthworks, paving had begun on the new road between Homesh and Sa-Nur, which bypasses the Palestinian village of Silat al-Dhahr. The road is meant to give safe, continuous travel between the re-established communities of northern Samaria. items.summary: Roy Kahlon, head of the Prime Minister’s Office task force against crime in the Arab sector, said that Arab crime organisations inside Israel now hold LAW anti-tank rockets, MAG machine guns, Claymore-type charges and explosive drones. items.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz told the cabinet that, beyond an attempt by terror groups to repeat 7 October, the security establishment is preparing for a complete reversal by the Palestinian Authority’s forces and the Tanzim militias. items.headline: Mass poisoning of a flock near the Allon Road
items.summary: Nine sheep and a sheepdog died, and more than forty sheep were harmed, after poison was poured into a water trough on a hilltop near the Allon Road in Binyamin. Residents said that the cell came from the direction of al-Mughayyir; the suspects have not been caught. Residents described it as the thirteenth poisoning of pastures along the Allon Road in the past year.

items.headline: Orders signed to demolish monuments glorifying terrorists
items.summary: Elchanan Groner reported that the IDF appears to be changing its policy on monuments glorifying terrorists, which until now required separate legal and command approval for each demolition. items.headline: Smuggler whose vehicle rammed an IDF Humvee is released
items.summary: Mahmoud Daisat, a known smuggler of illegal residents, was released on 6 October and handed to the Red Crescent as a free man. He had driven the vehicle that rammed an IDF Humvee in the Hebron hills on 5 October. Security officials expressed strong anger at the release and described the daily convoys of smugglers between the Hebron hills and the Negev as a serious danger; the IDF Spokesperson said

items.headline: Homes demolished at Ora Israel and Netzach Shmuel
items.summary: Border Police and Civil Administration inspectors in large numbers demolished four family homes at two settlement points, Ora Israel near Salfit and Netzach Shmuel near Adei Ad, and confiscated the flock of Ora Israel. Several teenagers were hurt by police and five were arrested. Residents describe Ora Israel as a barrier to Authority control of the Area A bloc between Salfit and Ramallah.

items.headline: Kfar Ana: drone footage shows Palestinians started the fire blamed on settlers
items.summary: Palestinians from Ein Yabrud set fire to a roadblock of tyres on the access road to Kfar Ana, between Beit El and Ofra, and the fire spread to a nearby Palestinian car lot. The village then said that settlers had set the lot alight. Drone footage shows the Palestinians beside the fire, and the IDF said that its trackers determined from the evidence that Palestinians had set it.

items.headline: Smotrich petitions the High Court to advance the E1 tender
items.summary: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich filed an urgent petition against an instruction by Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara to delay the opening of bids in the tender for 1,234 housing units in E1, at seven sites in the Mevaseret Adumim neighbourhood of Ma'ale Adumim. He said that political approval was given in October 2025, before the election period. He said that the building will connect Jerusale

items.headline: Children’s bus stoned on the Gilad road; poison spread on two pastures
items.summary: Arabs stoned a bus carrying children on the Gilad road in Samaria, the second attack on that road in two days. Attackers from Abu Falah spread poison on pastures near the Allon Road, and five sheep fell severely ill. Near Ma'ale Amos, in Gush Etzion, residents found dates laced with poison spread on their pastures by attackers from Kisan.

items.headline: Seventeen settlements approved in the Jenin district since early 2025
items.summary: According to figures from Peace Now cited by +972 Magazine, the government has approved 17 settlements in the Jenin district since the start of 2025, among them four evacuated in 2005; Ganim and Kadim have now been re-established, and Defence Minister Katz spoke at the ceremony for Ganim on 13 August. items.headline: Shin Bet chief raises the return of administrative detention against Jews
items.summary: David Zini, head of the Shin Bet, told the security cabinet that he may demand the return of administrative detention, imprisonment without charge or trial, against Jews in Judea and Samaria. Defence Minister Katz ended the use of such orders against Jews in November 2024, and any return rests with him. items.headline: Second attacker in the Hanina Farm stabbing attempt arrested
items.summary: The IDF announced that, after a joint pursuit under Shin Bet guidance, it arrested the second terrorist in the attempted stabbing near Kafr Rammun, together with a further suspect. Residents of the farm said that the first attacker set a vehicle alight and ran at them with a knife. One resident stopped him with his vehicle, and no Israelis were hurt.

items.headline: Two attempted attacks in Binyamin and the Hebron hills
items.summary: A terrorist with a knife came to the grazing land of Hanina Farm near Rammun, set fire to an Israeli vehicle and tried to stab residents, who stopped him with their vehicle. Earlier, near Bani Na'im east of Hebron, a vehicle carrying three Palestinians struck an IDF vehicle, and the soldiers fired. One occupant was killed and two were wounded; no soldiers or civilians were hurt.

items.headline: Minister Strook confronts the Shin Bet chief in the security cabinet
items.summary: Minister Orit Strook told the security cabinet that the security services give a partial picture of violence in Judea and Samaria, and that Palestinians attack shepherds and endanger their lives. Shin Bet head David Zini replied that Palestinians do not burn Jewish homes. items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that before an overnight operation in northern Samaria the IDF told the Palestinian Authority security services in advance, so that they would withdraw from the area. items.headline: Border Police prepare to demolish settlement points
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that Border Police carried out preparatory patrols for demolitions at no fewer than four settlement points, some of which house families. He criticised Brigadier General Kobi Heller for turning his forces against the settlements instead of against the organisers of disturbances during the olive harvest.

items.headline: Feiglin rejects the claim that armed settlers enter Arab villages to kill
items.summary: Moshe Feiglin, chairman of Zehut, challenged Gadi Eisenkot to give one name of an Arab whom a settler had deliberately gone to his village and murdered in the last ten years. He said that the Arabs killed in such incidents were terrorists who infiltrated communities and were stopped by the security forces or the emergency squads. He called Mr. Eisenkot’s account a gross lie and incitement.

items.headline: Hilltop communities seek recognition by the state, including in Areas A and B
items.summary: Residents of the new hilltop communities are campaigning before the elections for recognition and regularisation, including for communities in Areas A and B and on land registered as private. Shalhevet Goldstein of Givat Maoz Esther proposed cancelling the Oslo Accords, a new registration of all land, and the definition of a hilltop community as a security component that may be placed in Area B.

items.headline: Overnight raids in fourteen towns, and a general closure for 5 and 7 October
items.summary: Israeli forces raided at least fourteen villages and towns, arrested dozens of wanted men, and broke up a cell in Araneh, near Nablus, that was in advanced planning for an attack. In Awarta forces secured worshippers at the tombs of Eleazar and Ithamar. Defence Minister Katz ordered a general closure on Judea and Samaria on 5 and 7 October.

items.headline: False report of settler violence at Sebastia
items.summary: The main Nablus Telegram channel reported that settlers were attacking residents in Iyarib, Sebastia. Elisha Yered wrote after watching the video that the claim is false, and that footage presented as such an attack shows Jewish youths practising self-defence at the edge of a community.

items.headline: Four foreign activists face removal after olive-harvest provocations
items.summary: Four foreign activists who took part in a violent olive-harvest provocation in Gush Kana, in which Jewish youths were hurt, were detained by the IDF near Tapuah. They were questioned at the Ariel police station, and their file was sent to the Population and Immigration Authority for a hearing on removal from Israel. Yossi Dagan said that those who come to provoke must know that there is a price.

items.headline: Molotov attack on Eretz HaTzvi farm stopped by the owner
items.summary: Two attackers carrying Molotov cocktails came to Eretz HaTzvi farm near Nachliel, in western Binyamin, intending to set it on fire. The owner followed the arrest procedure, then fired and wounded one; no Israelis were hurt. The Palestinian Authority Health Ministry and WAFA presented the death of a 19-year-old from Kafr Aqab as a killing by settlers near Kobar.

items.headline: Wave of attacks in Samaria under cover of the olive harvest
items.summary: Near Nahal Kane and Tzon Aviezer, Arabs from Asira al-Qibliya attacked Jews and a Jewish youth was wounded in the head by a stone. Near Avnei Elad about fifty Arabs attacked settlers with stones, and Nahal Battalion 50 arrested five. Rioters from al-Mughayyir threw stones at a shepherd from Givat Or Nachman, and the IDF arrested two.

items.headline: Fatah and the anti-settlement committee prepare harvest riots in Binyamin
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that Fatah and the Committee Against Settlements held a long preparatory meeting in the Ramallah district with village Fatah secretaries. The meeting was held ahead of planned olive-harvest riots in Binyamin.

items.headline: About fifty terror suspects arrested during Sukkot
items.summary: During Sukkot the IDF, with Battalion 931 and the Maglan unit under the Samaria Brigade, arrested about fifty terror suspects, among them a Hamas activist in Nablus. Forces seized weapons, drones and materials for explosive devices, and struck a terrorist who tried to throw a charge at them.

items.summary: Dozens of Palestinians threw stones at a group of Israelis at a water cistern by the Anton farm, between Tapuach and Rechelim; police said a boy of about fourteen was lightly wounded and are examining a claim that attackers tried to drag one of the group toward the village. items.headline: Shepherd stoned by rioters from al-Mughayyir
items.summary: Dozens of rioters from al-Mughayyir, in Binyamin, attacked a Jewish shepherd from a nearby outpost with stones; he was not hurt. Witnesses said that the IDF response was weak, and that the village has grown more aggressive since the Paratroopers replaced the Duchifat Battalion in that sector.

items.headline: Olive pickers attack Beit Karnaim farm and try to seize the owner’s weapon
items.summary: Three Palestinians picking olives refused to leave the grazing land of Beit Karnaim farm near Maoz Tzur and threw stones at residents, wounding one in the head. They tried to seize the farm owner’s weapon, and he fired three shots into the air; one attacker was detained. The Binyamin Regional Council said that the harvest must not be used as cover for attacks.

items.headline: Dummy charge wrapped in a Hamas flag closes Route 463
items.summary: An object that looked like an explosive charge, wrapped in a Hamas flag, was placed on Route 463, the Wallerstein Road in Binyamin. The road was closed for about two hours until checks showed that it was a dummy.

items.headline: Thousands pray at Joseph’s Tomb with the Four Species
items.summary: Thousands entered Joseph’s Tomb in Nablus in two rounds with IDF approval, for the first mass morning prayer there with the Four Species in several decades. Senior commanders, members of Knesset and Yossi Dagan attended. Mr. Dagan and Zvi Sukkot called for the full return of the Od Yosef Chai yeshiva to the tomb.

items.headline: Warning that the Authority’s anti-settlement committee will use the olive harvest for attacks
items.summary: Elisha Yered wrote that the Arab olive harvest would open on 2 October and would be used for attacks near Jewish communities. He asked the commander of Central Command and the commander of the Judea and Samaria police district to arrest Mu'id Sha'aban and his group from the Palestinian Authority committee for fighting the settlements. This was a request, not a report of an arrest.

items.headline: Shepherd attacked near Maoz Tzur by about fifty masked men
items.summary: Four men attacked a Jewish shepherd at a farm near Maoz Tzur, and about fifty masked men from Beit Ur al-Tahta then joined them with clubs, stones and tear gas. Two Jews were hurt, and about one hundred metal spikes were found on an access road. About ninety minutes later some twenty men stoned a shepherd from the Metzudat David farm near al-Mughayyir.

items.headline: New settlement point, Golot, established near Otniel
items.summary: A new settlement point named Golot has been established in the Hebron hills, a few kilometres from Otniel, near the springs and Tel Devir. A road has been prepared, a metal structure placed, and a guard kept there day and night for two to three weeks. A group of families from Otniel and Tekoa is waiting to move in.

items.headline: Prayer at Beitunia square after the kidnapping of a reservist by Palestinian police
items.summary: Hundreds of residents of western Binyamin came in more than 80 vehicles to Beitunia square for morning prayers under IDF security. The organisers said it was a response to the kidnapping, about a month earlier and nearby, of an IDF reservist by terrorists from the Palestinian police. They called on the IDF and the government to restore control and security in the area.
