International service is still badly disrupted: Lufthansa and Air France have cancelled flights through mid-November (Gulf News). The reopening came on the same day as the Dammam attack and

items.headline: Britain commits RAF Typhoons to defend Saudi cities
items.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence said on Tuesday, 20 October, that RAF Typhoon jets will fly defensive counter-air missions to protect Saudi cities and critical infrastructure from Houthi missiles and drones. It stressed that the jets will not strike Houthi targets on the ground. Britain is also sending an A400M transport plane to move military equipment inside the kingdom and military advisers to work

items.headline: Turkey sends the Makkah defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to parliament
items.summary: President Erdogan on Tuesday submitted the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement, signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan on 7 August, to the Turkish parliament for ratification. Reuters (via Al-Monitor), Arab News, Daily Sabah and DW Turkish report it. According to Asharq Al-Awsat, the pact says an attack on one signatory is an attack on all three, like NATO's Article 5. The bill goes first to the f

items.headline: Shabwa camp toll rises to 73, the deadliest strike since the fighting resumed
items.summary: Shabwa's local authorities raised the death toll from Monday's Houthi ballistic-missile strike on the al-Alam training camp to 73, with 14 people still missing and more than 200 wounded (AP, AFP via Ahram Online, Saba via Iran International). Governor Awad bin al-Wazir told AP that the dead were all recruits aged 18 to 20 who were being trained for provincial security, not combat. AP calls it the

items.headline: Al-Alimi asks the UN to list the Houthis as terrorists and vows the offensive will go on
items.summary: Presidential Leadership Council head Rashad al-Alimi asked UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres by phone to back Security Council action designating the Houthis a terrorist organization, enforcing the arms embargo and cutting off their funding and weapons (Saba; Yemen foreign ministry; Asharq Al-Awsat). The reports of the call do not say that Guterres agreed. Meeting the US chargé d'affaires on T

items.headline: Riyadh: missile and drone intercepted, launcher destroyed
items.summary: Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki said on Tuesday that a Houthi ballistic missile fired at Riyadh was intercepted and destroyed, and later that evening a drone was shot down in the Riyadh region (Arab News, Al Arabiya, BBC Arabic). The coalition said it then destroyed the platform that launched the missile and released video of the strike (Qatar News Agency, Sabq). Saudi Civil Defense

items.headline: Fronts: Taiz attacks turned back, Marib under missile fire, doubts about the offensive
items.summary: On day 16 of Operation Dawn of Yemen, Asharq Al-Awsat and Al Jazeera report that government forces and the Popular Resistance turned back new Houthi attacks on the al-Shaqab front south of Taiz and kept fighting in Sanamat village in al-Misrakh district. Asharq Al-Awsat's field sources describe a lull in Houthi attacks on the city's edges that they read as regrouping for a bigger push. The Giants

items.headline: Iran says its mediation offer has gone unanswered and warns Egypt
items.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Iraq's Al Ekhbariya TV that neither Saudi Arabia nor the Houthis has answered Tehran's offer to broker talks. He said any foreign intervention "would complicate matters" and that Cairo had earlier told Tehran it would "not directly" interfere in Yemen (Reuters via The Jerusalem Post). That fits Yemen's rejection of Iranian mediation reported here yester

items.headline: Inside Saudi Arabia: AFP tallies the cost to Vision 2030
items.summary: An AFP analysis says the Houthi attacks threaten Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's plan to make the kingdom a hub for tourism, events and foreign business. A consultant to the Saudi government told AFP that the deeper risk is that company boards "start pricing Saudi as part of an active conflict zone." The IMF's October outlook, published on 13 October, expects the Saudi economy to shrink by 3.3

items.headline: Houthi missiles kill at least 53 recruits at a Shabwa training camp
items.summary: On Monday, 19 October, the Houthis fired three ballistic missiles at the al-Alam camp near Ataq, in Shabwa province, where recruits to the internal security forces and police were training, according to a spokesman for the government armed forces. Shabwa's local authority gave a preliminary toll of 53 killed and more than 200 injured, up from early reports of 18 dead. The deputy governor told AFP

items.headline: Saudi Arabia puts off its flagship investor conference until 2027
items.summary: The Future Investment Initiative, often called "Davos in the Desert," was due to open in Riyadh on 26 October. The FII Institute said on Monday that the tenth edition will take place in 2027 instead, with new dates to come; its notice does not mention the war. The Wall Street Journal and The National tie the decision to the Houthi missile and drone attacks on Riyadh, including King Khalid airport,

items.headline: Egypt's vote slips a full week, to 26 October, and some MPs push back
items.summary: Egypt's House of Representatives met in a second secret session on Monday and adjourned without voting on President el-Sisi's request for authority to support Saudi Arabia. Speaker Hisham Badawi set the next session for Monday, 26 October (Parlgate, Al-Qabas, and Reuters via Dawn; Al Jazeera confirms). That replaces the Tuesday vote reported here yesterday. Al-Masry Al-Youm, citing parliamentary s

items.headline: Houthis claim hits on Aramco in Yanbu, the Shaybah field and three airports
items.summary: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said on Monday that over the previous 48 hours the group carried out six operations with ballistic and cruise missiles and drones. He listed Aramco facilities in Yanbu, the Shaybah oil field, King Khalid airport in Riyadh, Abha airport, radars at Jabal al-Hisn, Jabal al-Rahma and Bir Askar, Khamis Mushait air base and a coalition naval camp, and claimed fires

items.headline: Fronts: government claims gains south of Taiz as the Houthis press the city
items.summary: On day 15 of Operation Dawn of Yemen, Asharq Al-Awsat, citing military sources, says government forces and the Popular Resistance advanced in the al-Sanamat and al-Sarari areas of Saber district, south of Taiz, after an offensive that began at dawn on Sunday. It says they also kept pressure on the remaining Houthi pockets around Bab al-Mandab and worked to secure the high ground between Taiz and L

items.headline: Pakistan says it is giving Saudi Arabia whatever support it needs
items.summary: Pakistan's military spokesman, Lt. Gen. Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry (DG ISPR), told Independent Arabia that the security of Saudi Arabia and the Two Holy Mosques is non-negotiable and that Pakistan is already providing whatever support the kingdom needs for its defense. He described the defense pact Pakistan signed with Saudi Arabia and Turkey as purely defensive, but said a collective response could fo

items.headline: Yemen's foreign minister rejects Iran as a mediator
items.summary: Foreign Minister Afrah Al-Zouba, speaking on the sidelines of an Organization of Islamic Cooperation foreign ministers' meeting in Baghdad, said Iran cannot arm the Houthis and then offer to mediate, and rejected Tehran's framing of the war as a Yemeni-Saudi conflict. She cited Iran's handover of Yemen's embassy in Tehran to a Houthi envoy in 2019 and flights to Sanaa in July 2026 without governme

items.headline: Egypt's vote moves to Tuesday; Egyptian transport planes tracked into Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Egypt's parliament ended Sunday's emergency session without voting on President el-Sisi's request for authority to defend Saudi Arabia, and resumes today, Monday 19 October. MP Mostafa Bakry, who is close to the state, wrote that debate will run three days because so many members asked to speak, with the vote expected on Tuesday (Ahram Online); Reuters and AFP confirm the delay. The pro-Sisi parti

items.headline: Gulf ministers back Saudi self-defense and call for the Houthis to be listed as terrorists
items.summary: The GCC Ministerial Council, meeting in Manama on Sunday for its 168th session, condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi airports and vital facilities, declared full solidarity with Saudi Arabia, and affirmed the individual and collective right of self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. It said the security of member states is indivisible, called for enforcement of the UN arms embargo, and u

items.headline: Saudi defense minister in Abu Dhabi as the UAE funding report stays unconfirmed
items.summary: Prince Khalid bin Salman, the Saudi defense minister, met UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed in Abu Dhabi on Sunday, with Vice President Mansour bin Zayed and national security adviser Tahnoon bin Zayed present. The official readouts from the UAE presidency and the Saudi Press Agency (via Asharq Al-Awsat) speak only of regional developments and priorities for the coming period. They do not mention Ye

items.headline: Houthis cut the main road from Aden into Taiz
items.summary: Yemen's transport ministry said the Houthis blew up a culvert on the road at Hayjat al-Abd, cutting the main route linking Taiz with Lahj and Aden. Al-Masdar Online reports the Houthis already control the area and that the road had reopened after an earlier blast, and Asharq Al-Awsat also reports the destruction. This matters for the campaign: it is the government side's main supply line into Taiz

items.headline: Fronts: Taiz lines hold, Bab al-Mandab mop-up, claimed push west of Marib
items.summary: Asharq Al-Awsat, citing military media, says government forces and the Popular Resistance turned back a broad Houthi attack west of Taiz and another on the al-Shaqab front at the city's southern entrance, while coalition jets struck around Jabal Han. On Sunday, the 14th day of Operation Dawn of Yemen, government forces began operations to clear Houthi pockets dug in behind hills, trenches and mine

items.headline: Houthis report 110 coalition strikes in a day
items.summary: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said 110 coalition strikes hit Sanaa and the provinces of Hodeidah, Taiz and Marib in 24 hours, killing or wounding more than 30 people (Xinhua). Houthi-run media now put the toll from Sunday's strike on a house in Saada's al-Tawila area at 10 dead and 23 wounded. The coalition has not commented on either claim, and neither can be checked.

items.headline: Riyadh: Kingdom Centre orders staff home, schools stay online, airport open only by permit
items.summary: The management of the Kingdom Centre tower in central Riyadh, whose tenants include Merrill Lynch, McKinsey and the IMF, told office staff on Sunday that remote work is mandatory 'until further notice,' in an email seen by AFP; the mall below stays open. Schools in Riyadh and the surrounding area extended online learning into a second week (AFP via Al-Monitor; Fox News). King Khalid International

items.headline: France: Barrot in Riyadh, Macron's Gulf tour skips Saudi Arabia
items.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot arrived in Riyadh on Sunday evening to restate French support for the kingdom (AFP via Al-Monitor; Sud Ouest). President Macron's tour from 19 to 21 October covers Kuwait, the UAE, Bahrain and Qatar, not Saudi Arabia, and is focused on securing fuel supplies and alternative shipping routes (France 24). France has already begun deploying military means to he

items.headline: No new overnight barrage reported yet
items.summary: As of about 5 a.m. in Israel on Monday, no coalition statement on overnight Houthi launches at Saudi Arabia could be found. Sunday's toll stands at two ballistic missiles intercepted near Khamis Mushait, three drones over Riyadh and the Eastern Province, and a projectile that hurt six people and damaged three homes and three vehicles in Najran (Saudi Civil Defense via Xinhua; AFP). Threat alerts f

items.headline: Egypt's parliament meets today on defending Saudi Arabia
items.summary: At a military academy graduation on Saturday, 17 October, President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi said Egypt would take any measure needed to protect Saudi Arabia if King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman ask, and asked parliament for an emergency session to authorize it. He said Egypt would act only in defense. Parliament's secretariat scheduled a plenary session for 1 p.m. Cairo time (1 p.m. in

items.headline: UAE reported to resume paying the Giants Brigades
items.summary: The Guardian reported on Saturday, citing sources in Yemen, that the UAE has agreed to resume funding southern forces, mainly the Giants Brigades it once trained and paid, in return for Saudi air support. Newsmax and Dunya News carry the report. The UAE left Yemen and stopped the payments in January after its dispute with Riyadh over the south. Neither government has confirmed the deal, so it is u

items.headline: New overnight barrage on Riyadh, the Eastern Province and Khamis Mushait
items.summary: Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki said early on Sunday, 18 October, that the coalition intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait and three drones, two over Riyadh region and one over the Eastern Province. Civil Defense sent alerts in Riyadh, Abha and Khamis Mushait before announcing the danger had passed. On Saturday the coalition had reported four drones downed

items.headline: Houthis claim a Saudi Apache shot down near Najran
items.summary: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said on Saturday that Houthi forces shot down a Saudi AH-64 Apache helicopter near Najran while it attacked their positions on the border. Video of a smoking aircraft is circulating on X, but it has not been verified, and Saudi officials have not commented. Anadolu reports the claim. It is unconfirmed. If true, it would be the first reported loss of a Saudi ai

items.headline: Taiz: government lines hold at Jabal Han, but no breakthrough
items.summary: Government forces said they repelled a Houthi assault west of Taiz city that lasted about 12 hours around Jabal Han, with fighting also at the old airport area, Ghurab and Bir Basha, and on the al-Dhabab, al-Aqrud and al-Shaqab fronts. Critical Threats, a US research project, reads the same reports as showing government forces holding the high ground west of the city that the Houthis have been try

items.headline: Former prime minister warns Taiz decides the whole west
items.summary: Maeen Abdelmalik Saeed, prime minister from 2018 to 2024 and now a presidential adviser, told The National that the Houthis are taking the rural outskirts and roads around Taiz before closing a full siege, and that losing the city would open the way to Aden, Marib and Lahj, home of one of Yemen's largest military camps. He said the government offensive holds the center of Mokha, but Houthi forces

items.headline: WSJ: Iranian officers directing Houthi strikes
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported on 16 October that Revolutionary Guard officers in Yemen helped the Houthis place missiles and radar near the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab, gave targeting intelligence for attacks on Saudi Arabia, and that some were on the front lines directing drone and missile attacks. Iran International and Saudi outlet Ajel carry the report. Iran denies encouraging the attacks; th

items.headline: Riyadh airport: no reopening announced
items.summary: The notice closing King Khalid International Airport expired at 2100 GMT on Saturday (midnight in Riyadh and in Israel). As of early Sunday, no reopening announcement from the Saudi civil aviation authority could be found in the reports checked; AGBI had said before the deadline that the notice could easily be extended, and Asiatoday reports that no date has been given. That status is unconfirmed

items.headline: Evening: Egypt's defense council pledges support to Saudi Arabia; parliament puts off its vote to Monday
items.summary: Egypt's National Defence Council, chaired by President el-Sisi, pledged on Sunday 'all necessary and possible forms of support' to Saudi Arabia and said the kingdom's security is linked to Egypt's own. The statement did not mention troops, but MP Mostafa Bakry, who is close to the state, wrote that the council approved sending forces on 'a defensive mission'; that is his claim. Parliament met in a

items.headline: Evening: Saudi Arabia says the Najran helicopter crashed from a malfunction; Houthi video appears to show it hit
items.summary: Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki said on Sunday that a Saudi National Guard AH-6i reconnaissance helicopter crashed inside Saudi territory in the Najran region 'due to a technical malfunction,' killing its two officers (Arab News; Al Arabiya). The Houthis had claimed on Saturday that they shot down an 'Apache' near Najran. Video they later released appears to show a small helicopter c

items.headline: Evening: Houthi projectile hurts six in a residential area of Najran
items.summary: Saudi Civil Defense said a projectile fired by the Houthis hit a residential area in Najran, injuring six Saudi citizens and damaging homes (Okaz; Sabq). It was one of several attacks on the south of the kingdom on Sunday. Saudi Arabia later lifted its warnings for the southern and southwestern regions (Anadolu).

items.headline: Evening: Houthi media say a Saudi strike on a house in Saada killed nine
items.summary: The Houthi agency Saba said a Saudi airstrike on a home in Saada province killed nine people and wounded 16, 'most of them women and children,' and that the toll was not final (AFP via Dawn). Later Houthi-linked reports gave 10 dead and 23 wounded. The figures come only from the Houthis; the coalition has not commented, and what the strike targeted is not known.

items.headline: Evening: Riyadh airport reopens, but most foreign airlines stay away
items.summary: The National reports that King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh reopened on Sunday after its closure because of Houthi attacks. Many carriers have not resumed: Qatar Airways and Air Arabia gave no date, Oman Air is suspended until 22 October, Air France and Air India until 24 October, KLM until 31 October, Lufthansa until 18 November, and Cathay Pacific until 31 January. No Saudi official st

items.headline: Evening: Aden airport reopens; the Cairo flight diversion is confirmed
items.summary: Aden International Airport resumed traffic on Saturday, 17 October. The Yemeni sites Al-Wajha and Anbaa Aden report that a Fly Aden (Aden Airways) flight from Cairo circled over Aden for more than an hour during Friday night's attack, diverted to Djibouti, and later landed in Aden. That confirms the diversion this page marked as unconfirmed this morning. No official damage assessment of the airpor

items.headline: Evening: Coalition says it destroyed two missile launchers in Saada
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said that early on Saturday it destroyed two ballistic-missile launch platforms in Saada province and stopped a sea smuggling attempt toward Hodeidah. Its spokesman, Turki al-Maliki, posted video. Asharq Al-Awsat, Anadolu and CNN Arabic report the statement. The Houthis have not commented, and the results are confirmed only by the coalition. The coalition also said King Kha

items.headline: Evening: Houthis say Saudi strike in Dhamar killed three children
items.summary: The Houthi-run health ministry said a Saudi airstrike on 16 October on the villages of al-Ar and Barza'a, in Dawran Anis district of Dhamar province, killed three children and wounded 15 to 17 people. The Houthi agency Saba says cluster bombs were used; that is unconfirmed. AP, reported by the Times of Israel, says Saudi Arabia did not comment, and that the Houthis say 124 people have been killed

items.headline: Evening: Riyadh airport reopening still unconfirmed
items.summary: As of Saturday evening there was no Saudi announcement that King Khalid International Airport will reopen when the notice to airmen expires at 2100 GMT, or midnight in Riyadh and in Israel. Gulf Business and AGBI report the notice and the uncertainty. Airlines are extending suspensions: IndiGo and Akasa Air have cancelled Saudi flights until 24 October, and Air India until 20 October. Reports in s

items.headline: Two missiles land inside Aden airport
items.summary: On Friday night, 16 October, two missiles landed inside Aden International Airport, police and government officials said, blaming the Houthis. Reports say one landed about 500 meters from a Yemenia aircraft; passengers and crew were evacuated and no casualties were reported in early accounts. A Houthi military source told the Houthi-run Saba agency that the target was a Saudi forces command headqu

items.headline: Government says it will stay in Aden
items.summary: Marwan Ali Noman, political adviser to Foreign Minister Afrah Al Zouba, told The National the government will keep operating from Aden despite the palace strike, and remains committed to Operation Dawn of Yemen. The Health Ministry now puts the palace toll at five security personnel killed and 16 injured, a figure the BBC also carries from Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani. An unnamed governm

items.headline: Intercepts over Yanbu, the Red Sea and Riyadh
items.summary: Coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said on Friday that a ballistic missile fired toward the Red Sea oil hub of Yanbu was intercepted, along with two cruise missiles over the Red Sea and three drones over the Riyadh and southern regions, plus a drone aimed at the Eastern Province. Asharq Al-Awsat, The National and AFP report the statements. On Thursday the coalition said it shot down a cru

items.headline: Coalition strikes smuggling targets at Hodeidah
items.summary: The coalition released aerial footage dated 16 October of strikes it says hit a Houthi weapons-smuggling operation at the port of Hodeidah, including boats and storage sites. Al-Maliki posted the video on X. The coalition gave no detail on the targets, the weapons or the damage, so the results are unconfirmed. Arab News reports the release.

items.headline: Army claims further gains in Marib; Taiz attacks repelled
items.summary: The Yemeni army said on Friday it widened its breakthrough on the eastern front in Marib and took several positions and high ground, without naming them; some outlets place the push in Raghwan district near the Mas camp, which controls roads toward Sanaa. It claimed more than 430 Houthi fighters killed or disabled and over 100 vehicles destroyed in 24 hours; those figures are unverified and the Ho

items.headline: Trump says Riyadh will accept Israeli help
items.summary: Asked on Friday at the White House whether Saudi Arabia should accept Israel's offer of help against the Houthis, President Trump said, "Yes, I think so," and that "Israel has been very helpful to Saudi Arabia." He did not say what help Israel had given. He added that Saudi entry into the Abraham Accords was back on the table, "perhaps now more than ever." The Jerusalem Post, The Times of Israel a

items.headline: Security Council backs Saudi right of self-defense
items.summary: On 15 October the UN Security Council adopted a presidential statement (S/PRST/2026/4) strongly condemning the Houthi attacks on Saudi airports and Aramco facilities, affirming Saudi Arabia's right of self-defense, and calling for action to stop arms reaching the Houthis. The Saudi foreign ministry welcomed it on Friday and stressed resolution 2216. The UN press office and Asharq Al-Awsat both rep

items.headline: Riyadh airport closure runs out tonight
items.summary: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh stayed closed on Friday. The current notice to airmen runs until midnight local time on 17 October, but aviation outlets including AGBI say reopening is in doubt and the Saudi authorities have not confirmed a date. Air India has halted flights to several Saudi cities until 20 October, according to posts on X; that is not independently confirmed.

items.headline: Missiles hit Maashiq Palace in Aden
items.summary: On 15 October the Houthis fired missiles, and according to the cabinet also drones, at Al-Maashiq Palace, the seat of Yemen's internationally recognized government in Aden. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani and cabinet members were unharmed and that two of the prime minister's escorts were killed. Yemen's health minister told Reuters five people were kille

items.headline: Coalition says it destroyed 127 mountain depots
items.summary: Coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said the alliance had destroyed 127 Houthi mountain storage facilities and several launch platforms in recent days, in response to attacks on Saudi airports and other sites. He put the toll from 20 attacks on King Khalid airport in Riyadh at 17 dead and 333 wounded, and three dead and 28 wounded at Abha. The National and Reuters both carry the briefing.

items.headline: Aramco operations and shipping still running
items.summary: Reuters sources say Aramco's Dhahran headquarters suffered extensive fire damage, including floors near the CEO's office, but that operations at the complex continued normally, with some staff working from home and some functions moved to global offices. TradeWinds separately reported that Aramco's maritime shipping kept running. No confirmed disruption to crude production or exports from the Dhah

items.headline: France begins deploying to protect Yanbu; EU-GCC summit postponed
items.summary: France said it had begun putting into action military means under an agreement to help protect Saudi oil facilities, including at the Red Sea export hub of Yanbu. The French foreign ministry did not detail the assets. Britain has already flown an RAF Voyager tanker on Saudi-linked missions; Italy has previously supplied radars and batteries. A planned EU-GCC summit in Riyadh set for 24 October has

items.headline: Taiz fighting continues; five Houthi officials captured
items.summary: Asharq Al-Awsat reports that Operation Dawn of Yemen entered its tenth day with heavy fighting west and south of Taiz, including at al-Dhabab, al-Aqroud and al-Shaqab, and pressure around Jabal Han. The Fifth Presidential Guard Brigade said it captured five Houthi security officials west of Taiz; Houthi prisoner-affairs official Abdulqader al-Murtada acknowledged Interior Ministry employees were h

items.headline: Aramco headquarters building hit in Dhahran
items.summary: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy said a missile struck an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran on Tuesday evening, causing a limited fire and no casualties. Bloomberg and a company source quoted by Reuters described the site as Aramco's executive or headquarters complex; the ministry did not name the building. The National and Al Jazeera both report the ministry confirmation. Yahya Saree had

items.headline: More intercepts over Riyadh; airport still closed
items.summary: The coalition says it intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh on Wednesday; Civil Defense said debris from intercepted missiles injured four people and damaged homes. Yahya Saree claimed a precise hit on King Khalid airport; Saudi authorities have not confirmed that claim. The airport remains closed through 17 October.

items.headline: STC mass rally held in Aden
items.summary: Tens of thousands gathered at Al-Aroud Square in Aden on 14 October for the Southern Transitional Council's mass mobilization, answering Aidarous al-Zubaidi's call. Parallel events were held in Shabwa, Hadramout, Al-Mahra and Socotra. A rally statement condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi civilians and called for recognition of an independent southern state, while limiting southern forces' role to de

items.headline: Heavy fighting on several Taiz fronts
items.summary: Fighting continued west and south of Taiz, at al-Dhabab, Al-Aqrud, Al-Shaqab and the Dhubab axis. The Taiz Military Axis claimed more than 200 Houthi fighters killed or wounded on Wednesday; the figure is unverified and the Houthis have not commented. Asharq Al-Awsat reports government claims of thousands of precision strikes under Dawn of Yemen and continued pressure on the Al-Waziiyah and Al-Mud

items.headline: Six Kings Slam postponed in Riyadh
items.summary: Organizers postponed the Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition in Riyadh from late October to late December, citing organizational and logistical challenges. Multiple outlets link the move to the Houthi attacks and security concerns. The Future Investment Initiative conferences had earlier been said to be going ahead.

items.headline: Coalition strikes Houthi fuel sites; Houthis threaten Saudi oil
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition struck Houthi-held energy sites, including the Al Sabahah fuel station in Sanaa and fuel-loading piers at Hodeidah. The Houthis answered by declaring Saudi oil installations legitimate targets and telling workers to stay away.

items.headline: Government claims new ground in Marib
items.summary: Under the Dawn of Yemen operation, government forces claim the heights around Maas camp in Medghal, in the northwest, and al-Muqailat and Jabal Zajjar north of Harib. Some Yemeni outlets say Maas camp itself fell; Al Jazeera reported only the surrounding heights. Independent confirmation of the camp is thin.

items.headline: Fighting continues west of Taiz
items.summary: Fighting continues on the western approaches, at al-Dhabab and nearby. Government sources claim dozens of Houthi fighters were captured at al-Dhabab. Al-Waziiya remains the choke point toward the Mocha coast.

items.headline: Three missiles intercepted; Riyadh airport still closed
items.summary: The coalition says it intercepted three missiles aimed at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait. King Khalid airport in Riyadh is still closed through 17 October; streets and offices there are otherwise reported as normal.

items.headline: Saudi air defenses under strain
items.summary: Officials told AP that the kingdom is investigating how Saturday's barrage reached Riyadh; drones were sent ahead of cruise and ballistic missiles. The Wall Street Journal reports that interceptors are running low and batteries are being moved to protect energy sites and palaces. Riyadh airport stays closed until 17 October. The coalition says it intercepted missiles aimed at Riyadh and Khamis Mus

items.headline: Saudi agencies raise readiness
items.summary: The information minister said all state agencies have raised their readiness, that life continues normally, and that citizens should not share unofficial footage.

items.headline: Trump speaks with the Crown Prince; no decision
items.summary: President Trump spoke with the Crown Prince on Monday and said the Houthis are "misbehaving very badly," but announced no decision. Iran offered to help start Saudi-Houthi talks; no Saudi reply is reported. Haaretz reports that the Crown Prince refused an Israeli request to join the campaign.

items.headline: Fighting reaches al-Dhabab, the entrance to Taiz
items.summary: The fighting is now at al-Dhabab, the city's southwestern entrance. Government military reports say the Houthis can fire on the al-Dhabab road. Government forces say they retook several hills there. The Houthis have not commented.

items.headline: Houthi attack in Lahj toward the coast road
items.summary: Government-aligned media say the Houthis are attacking in al-Madaraba toward the coast road that supplies the Bab al-Mandab front.

items.headline: Riyadh airport struck again
items.summary: A projectile struck Terminal 4 at King Khalid airport on 11 October and started a fire. The civil aviation authority says one person was killed and eleven were wounded. The airport remains closed. Saturday's death toll has risen to 13 after an Indian citizen died of his wounds.

items.headline: Houthis claim the strikes; Saudi defenses intercept more
items.summary: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed Saturday's strike, and also claimed hits on Dammam airport and two Aramco facilities. Saudi Arabia and Aramco have not confirmed the Aramco claim. The coalition reports intercepting a cruise missile near Riyadh, a drone over the Eastern Province and a ballistic missile aimed at Khamis Mushait. Civil defense alerts sounded in Abha.

items.headline: Riyadh conferences will go ahead
items.summary: Reuters reports that organizers say the major Riyadh conferences, including the Future Investment Initiative on 26 to 29 October, will go ahead.

items.headline: New attack at al-Wazi'iyah, west of Taiz
items.summary: The Giants Brigades and Nation's Shield say they opened a new attack at al-Wazi'iyah and repelled a Houthi push toward Dhubab airport. The Houthis have not commented. The government says the main roads into Taiz are open, but its own health ministry describes the siege as tightening. Government sources say aircraft are now targeting Houthi supply routes around the city.
